text.text_excerpt: The Cellars fills an essential need to this suburban community, a place to buy wines (and liquor) that may not be available in the local grocery stores. (Yes, grocery stores sell liquor in NOLA). They have a good selection and sponsor tastings most Friday nights, which my uncle is a big fan of. They have also sponsored seasonal dinners, which my parents have said were quite tasty. A bit off the beaten path for me, but I am always willing to trek out there with various family members who live in the area. They also have a deli counter which I really need to go try, especially since I recently heard that a cousin is managing it. Prices are competitive.

I enjoyed walking into the Cellars of River Ridge tonight. I looked to the right at the wine bar and to the left at the tables for the deli. Plenty of people, quite a few friends and neighbors. It's Friday night, time for the weekly wine tasting. This week it was J Lohr's Carol's Vineyard Sauvignon Blanc, Fog's Reach Arroyo Seco Pinot Noir, and Hilltop Cabernet Sauvignon. Last week is was four Decoy wines from Duckhorn Vineyards. The prior week included the Swanson Merlot, among others. Great place to get a glass (or bottle) of wine and some tapas if you are just wanting a short night out or to socialize if planning to start something a bit longer. The Deli serves some great food. This a is a good little neighborhood wine cellar. They have a small selection, but everything they have is quality. If they don't have something, they'll be happy to order it for you. It's a little pricey, but it is convenient, the staff is helpful, and it has a good atmosphere inside. Wine tastings on friday afternoon/evening also.
